from.place: Tag 08EV proof: finite Tor dimension together with pseudo-coherence implies perfectness

title: Pseudo-coherent complexes of finite Tor dimension are perfect
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let K be a pseudo-coherent object of D(\mathcal O_S) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. If K has finite Tor dimension, then K is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex].

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 20.49.5 (Tag 08CQ; label cohomology-lemma-perfect)

proof.text: Read the hypothesis as in its citers: there are integers a <= b with H^i(K \otimes^L_{\mathcal O_S} \mathcal F)=0 for every \mathcal O_S-module \mathcal F and every i outside [a,b]. Perfectness is local on the scheme by [def-pc-perfect-complex], and by the local definition [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] there is an open cover of S on whose members K is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free modules; refine it to a cover by affine opens V = Spec(R), on which the same holds. For an \mathcal O_V-module G, with j: V -> S the inclusion, part (1) of [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde] gives (K \otimes^L j_*G)|_V \cong K|_V \otimes^L_{\mathcal O_V} G, so H^i(K|_V \otimes^L G)=0 for i outside [a,b].

source.place: Lemma 20.49.5 (Tag 08CQ), proof: locality on the scheme

proof.text: On V = Spec(R) let K|_V \cong F^\bullet with F^\bullet a bounded-above complex of finite free \mathcal O_V-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] (with N = R) the global sections of \mathcal O_V are R, so \mathcal O_V^n = \widetilde{R^n} and each differential \mathcal O_V^{n} -> \mathcal O_V^{m} is a matrix over R; hence F^\bullet = \widetilde{P^\bullet} for a bounded-above complex P^\bullet of finite free R-modules. The construction \widetilde{(-)} is exact (its sections over the basic opens D(r) are localizations, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]) and \widetilde M = 0 only for M = 0 (global sections recover M). For an R-module M, part (3) of [lem-pc-affine-derived-pullback-tensor-tilde] gives \widetilde{P^\bullet} \otimes^L \widetilde M \cong \widetilde{P^\bullet \otimes^L_R M}, so by Step 1 applied to G = \widetilde M and exactness, H^i(P^\bullet \otimes^L_R M) = 0 for i outside [a,b]. Thus C = P^\bullet satisfies the hypotheses of the ring criterion [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect], which gives an isomorphism in D(R) between P^\bullet and a bounded complex E^\bullet of finitely generated projective R-modules.

source.place: Lemma 20.49.5 (Tag 08CQ), proof: reduce to the affine case and apply More on Algebra, Lemma 15.76.2 (Tag 0658)

proof.text: Since \widetilde{(-)} is exact (Step 2) it carries the quasi-isomorphisms of a roof between P^\bullet and E^\bullet to quasi-isomorphisms, so K|_V \cong \widetilde{P^\bullet} \cong \widetilde{E^\bullet} in D(\mathcal O_V). Each E^i is a direct summand of some R^n, so \widetilde{E^i} is a direct summand of \mathcal O_V^n and \widetilde{E^\bullet} is strictly perfect; hence K|_V is perfect by [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Since this holds on every member of the affine cover, K is perfect on S.
